resolution.rationale: First stable sync of this patch. Upstream v0.95.0 (#1262) adds the AIR capability backgroundSubagents, which ends an ACP v1 prompt turn at its result while background subagents still run, the same purpose as settleAtResult. It gates turnAwaitingSubagents on a new endsTurnsWithLiveSubagents(), the line this patch edits, so 5e5dd2485e577189dee329e860f0f7368bf1de2f conflicts. The same gate also keeps the streamed tool input of live subagents when such a turn ends, and drops the clear-context option from an ExitPlanMode request made out of a turn. The replacement routes settleAtResult through endsTurnsWithLiveSubagents() instead of short-circuiting turnAwaitingSubagents, so an opted-in client also gets upstream's out-of-turn handling. The wire contract is unchanged: the opt-in is clientCapabilities._meta.settleAtResult: true and the answer is _meta.settleAtResult.supported. Like backgroundSubagents it now applies to ACP v1 only: an ACP v2 session keeps the hold and is not advertised the extension. This matters because since #1400 the adapter speaks ACP v2 to any client that asks for protocol version 2 or later; that is recorded, not changed, here. The patch is not absorbed, because backgroundSubagents is read only from the AIR declaration. Three new tests fail with a plain replay of the original gate and pass with the replacement: the streamed input of a running subagent still refines its tool call after the response, an out-of-turn ExitPlanMode request has no clear-context option, and ACP v2 does not advertise the extension. The original test passes with both. The replacement has a stable patch-id distinct from every ledger and retired commit.
